data.narrative:
Array Labs is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Andrew Peterson and Jose Isaac Robledo that has raised $35M to date. The valuation exercise benchmarks against a universe of 13 comparable companies: 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression anchoring is sufficiently supported by available data. This method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to growth-stage transitions, using the $35M raised as a proxy base value and yielding $70M. The peer-median approach cannot be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector (only 2 adjacent-stage peers identified, below the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical validity). Public-comp anchoring via EV/Sales multiples is inapplicable because Array Labs' revenue is not publicly disclosed—a standard limitation for private company analysis.

The triangulated valuation range of $60M to $80M reflects stage-progression methodology with conservative and optimistic case adjustments, centering on a $70M median. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, which prevents calibration against the 23.9x median P/S multiple observed in public Space & Aerospace comparables, and limited private-peer data at the exact Series A stage. A future valuation would benefit materially from revenue disclosure or access to a denser set of same-stage private transactions.
